question.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(2)+{f}^{′}(2)(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $f(2)=5,$ and since ${f}^{′}(x)=3{x}^{2}-2x,$ we have

$$
{f}^{′}(2)=3(2)^{2}-2(2)=12-4=8.
$$

So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
L(x)=5+8(x-2).
$$

Now, we can approximate $f(2.4)$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=2.4.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2.4) & ≈L(2.4) \\  & =5+8(2.4-2) \\  & =5+8(0.4) \\  & =5+3.2 \\  & =8.2.\end{aligned}
$$
